newsitem.title: UK: ANZ to lead manage Eurobond for Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: ANZ to lead manage Eurobond for Pakistan.

text.p: ANZ Investment Bank said on Thursday it had been mandated to lead a three-year Eurobond issue for the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
The deal will be roadshowed in mid-March and launch is expected before the end of March.
In a statement, ANZ said: "The bullet maturity bond will represent the first opportunity for investors to gain new Government of Pakistan exposure following the election on February 3."
ANZ said the economic programme agreed between the previous caretaker administration and the IMF was expected to remain in place.
ANZ said it was the largest foreign bank operating in Pakistan.
ANZ new issues syndicate official Jo Cunningham said further details of the Eurobond were not yet finalised but that it would be a benchmark dollar transaction for the borrower.

In December 1994 Pakistan launched a $150 million 11.50 percent December 1999 bond. It was launched to yield 385 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes and was last trading at 415 b.p. over, traders said.
Cunningham said this issue, however, was adversely affected by the Mexican peso crisis.
Pakistan is rated B2 by Moody's Investors Service and B+ by Standard & Poor's Corp.
